d response\nspellings. Each one answers with `Deprecation: true` and a `Link` header naming\nits successor. They are undocumented

on purpose — the spec is what a new
integration reads — and they are removed at general availability.

A handful of operations
kept their names through the rename and so have no\ndeprecated twin to hold the old field spellings. `get_swarms_overview`,\n`crea

te_swarm` and `update_swarm` emit both and accept either — never both in

### Vocabul

ary

A name can move behind an alias; a VALUE cannot. `sourceType` is one field with
one string in it, and a client switching o

n `"scenario"` has no second name to
fall back to. So the values negotiate.

Send `x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary: 2` and the rename

d values read canonically:

| Field | Vocabulary 1 | Vocabulary 2 |
| - | - | - |
| session `sourceType` | `scenario` | `study
` |\n| session `parentRef.kind` | `scenario`, `journeyRun` | `study`, `goalRun` |\n| session `parentRef` ids | `scenarioId`, `jour
neyRunId`, `journeyRefId` | `studyId`, `goalRunId`, `goalRefId` |\n| share `resourceType` (field AND path segment) | `scenario` |

`study` |
| trace-destination `sourceTypes` | `scenario` | `study` |

Absent means `1`, which is byte-for-byte today's contract
. Any other value is a\n`400`. On the way IN, a vocabulary-2 request may name a filter or a path segment\nby either spelling; a vo
cabulary-1 request may use only the legacy one, because\na boundary that accepts a spelling it does not announce is one two\nimple

mentations can disagree about. A response that varies by vocabulary sends
`Vary: x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary`.

This is a **separat
e header** from `x-mcpjam-eval-vocabulary`, which is\neval-scoped by name and moves on its own schedule. A deployment may speak on

e
and not the other, so read
`GET /projects/{projectId}/capabilities` — `apiVocabulary` and `vocabulary` are
two blocks — befor
e sending either. With the SDK:\n`new PlatformApiClient({ …, apiVocabulary: 2 })`, or\n`client.withApiVocabulary(2)` on one you al

ready hold.

Permalink resource types are the exception that proves the rule: `study` and
`goal_run` are the canonical keys, `u
ser_testing_scenario` and `journey_run`\nstill resolve to the same routes, and which one a response carries follows the\nOPERATION
rather than the header — a renamed operation derives the canonical\nkey, its deprecated twin the old one. `capabilities.apiVocabu

lary.resourceTypes`
lists both.

### Browser tools on chat sessions

> [!NOTE]
>
> Hosted browser availability depends on t
he account and deployment. The browser workspace must be enabled to open the live pane in the Playground.\n\n`POST /chat-sessions/
messages` accepts an optional `browser: { policy?, profileId? }`. Attach it on every turn that should browse. The initial grant an
d profile are fixed; the current host policy and pinned read-only mode can narrow the effective permissions. Responses and traces
include the read-only `chatSessionId`, browser metadata, and screenshot URLs without inline image data.\n\n| Method | Path | Purpo
se |\n| - | - | - |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/browser` | Create an empty API session and its browser with `projectId`, `policy`, o
ptional `profileId`, and a stable `idempotencyKey`. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/open` | Open or wake the sessi
on browser. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/command` | Execute a browser command under the session policy with a s
table `commandId`. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/note` | Append a command-ledger note. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessio
ns/{sessionId}/browser/trace` | Read command receipts and screenshot evidence. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/art
ifact` | Resolve a command screenshot URL. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/close` | Release the session desktop. |
\n\nOnly the owning user can drive an API session's browser. All inputs use the public `sessionId`; conversation and browser ident
ifiers in responses are informational. Capacity refusals before execution release the turn lease so the same idempotency key can b

e retried. An execution with an unknown outcome must be inspected before attempting a new action.
